newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond market focuses on new issues.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond market focuses on new issues.

text.p: The investment grade U.S. corporate bond market was quiet and directionless on Wednesday, as market players continued to focus on new issues, traders said.
"The market is trying to get some leadership from new issues," said one trader. "If new deals break down, it won't bode well for the market."

Prices on recently price new high-grade paper held firm, but did little to provide direction to the market. Deutsche Bank Financial's $550 million 12-year offering that was priced on Tuesday, was issue bid, traders said.
Barrick Gold's $500 million 10-year debtentures, also priced yesterday, were trading at par on Wednesday, traders said.
Investment-grade issuers tapped the market with over $1 billion in new paper on Wednesday.
Societe Generale sold $400 million of step-up perpetual notes in a 144a offering via Morgan Stanley & Co. The notes, rated A1/A, were priced to yield 7.87 percent.
Kroger Co, a supermarket chain, sold $200 million in 10-year senior notes via Goldman Sachs & Co. The notes, which were rated Baa3/BBB-, were priced to yield 7.673 percent.

Tenneco Inc, a manufacturer specializing in auto parts and packaging, sold $100 million in 10-year notes to yield 7.551 percent and $200 million in 30-year notes to yield 8.074 percent. Merrill Lynch & Co was the lead underwriter for the deal.

Similar to high-grade corporate bonds, the secondary market for junk bonds also saw little trading on Wednesday. Despite weakness in the Treasury and equity markets, junk bond prices remained unchanged on the day, traders said.
Neenah Corp sold $150 million in senior subordinated notes in a 144a offering via Chase Securities Inc late on Wednesday.
The deal was increased from an original size of $140 million and priced at the inside of price talk at 11.125 percent, sources said. The notes were rated B3/B-.
Proceeds from the offering will be used to finance a leveraged buyout of the company.
Neenah, based in Neenah Wisc, manufactures iron casting such as manhole covers and sewer grates.
Over $700 million in new junk bonds are expected to price by the end of the week, syndicate sources said.
Elsewhere, Moody's Investors Service cut the rating of CSX Corp senior unsedured debt to Baa2 from Baa1.

Investors are likely to use the move to demand a higher yield on CSX's $2 billion debt offering expected to hit the market in several weeks, syndicate officials said. Traders said they could not determine if prices on outstanding CSX paper were affected because the bond rarely trade.

Moody's said the action was the result of weakened debt protection measurements at CSX following financing of its share of the acquisition of Conrail as well as increased competitive pressures in Conrail's territory.
CSX has agreed to acquire 42 percent of Conrail's assets, while Norfolk Southern Corp will acquire 58 percent.
In the Treasury market, the price of the 30-year bond dropped 16/32 to 94-10/32, yielding 7.08 percent. The price of the benchmark 10-year dropped 10/32 to 95-18/32, to yield 6.88 percent.
